granovetter1973strength.title: The Strength of Weak Ties
granovetter1973strength.abstract_or_role: Weak ties can carry information across groups; strong ties are associated with overlap within communities. Theoretical background only.

freeman1977set.title: A Set of Measures of Centrality Based on Betweenness
freeman1977set.abstract_or_role: Betweenness centrality: the share of shortest paths between other node pairs that pass through a node. Not a sufficient test of Burt brokerage.

gould1989structures.title: Structures of Mediation: A Formal Approach to Brokerage in Transaction Networks
gould1989structures.authors: Gould, Roger V. and Fernandez, Roberto M.
gould1989structures.abstract_or_role: Five brokerage roles defined on directed open two-paths (s->v->t with no direct s->t tie), combined with group membership.

burt1992structural.title: Structural Holes: The Social Structure of Competition
burt1992structural.abstract_or_role: Structural holes: non-redundant contacts in an ego network give information and control benefits. Defines network constraint.

newman2001scientific.title: Scientific collaboration networks. {I}. Network construction and fundamental results
newman2001scientific.abstract_or_role: Co-authorship collaboration networks built from article-author two-mode data and projected to one mode. In this paper, co-authorship is not treated as direct evidence of knowledge flow.

burt2004structural.title: Structural Holes and Good Ideas
burt2004structural.abstract_or_role: Managers who span structural holes have better ideas; brokerage needs real ties and observed outcomes.

opsahl2013triadic.title: Triadic closure in two-mode networks: Redefining the global and local clustering coefficients
opsahl2013triadic.abstract_or_role: One-mode projection of two-mode networks creates artificial closure; clustering must be redefined for two-mode data.

jasny2015two.title: Two-mode brokerage in policy networks
jasny2015two.abstract_or_role: Two-mode brokerage chains with group heterogeneity, as an alternative to computing brokerage after projection.

everett2020unpacking.title: Unpacking {Burt}'s constraint measure
everett2020unpacking.authors: Everett, Martin G. and Borgatti, Stephen P.
everett2020unpacking.abstract_or_role: Burt's constraint is driven by degree and dyadic ties; it is not a simple 0-1 index of exclusive brokerage.

saglietto2020research.title: Research on Structural Holes: An Assessment on Measurement Issues
saglietto2020research.authors: Saglietto, Laurence and C{\'e}zanne, C{\'e}cile and David, Delphine
saglietto2020research.abstract_or_role: Review of measurement issues in structural-hole research: different measures suit different data types and cannot be substituted arbitrarily.

zador2022weighted.title: A Weighted and Normalized {Gould--Fernandez} brokerage measure
zador2022weighted.authors: Z{\'a}dor, Zs{\'o}fia and Zhu, Zhen and Smith, Matthew and Gorgoni, Sara
zador2022weighted.abstract_or_role: Weighted and normalised Gould-Fernandez brokerage measure that avoids information loss from dichotomisation.

johnson2026reassessing.title: Reassessing Constraint's Meaning: A Framework for Reinterpreting Structural Holes' Findings
johnson2026reassessing.authors: Johnson, John Chandler and Sasson, Amir
johnson2026reassessing.abstract_or_role: Network constraint operationalises mainly dyadic constructs (alternatives, partner diversity, concentration) rather than broader network structure. A reinterpretation framework for structural-hole findings, not a refutation of the theory.

dempe2002foundations.title: Foundations of Bilevel Programming
dempe2002foundations.abstract_or_role: Foundations of bilevel programming: hierarchy, non-unique follower responses, optimistic and pessimistic formulations.

colson2007overview.title: An overview of bilevel optimization
colson2007overview.authors: Colson, Beno{\^\i}t and Marcotte, Patrice and Savard, Gilles
colson2007overview.abstract_or_role: Overview of bilevel optimisation formulations and solution approaches, including MPEC.

fortunyamat1981representation.title: A Representation and Economic Interpretation of a Two-Level Programming Problem
fortunyamat1981representation.venue: Journal of the Operational Research Society
fortunyamat1981representation.abstract_or_role: KKT/complementarity reformulation of two-level programming problems.

jeroslow1985polynomial.title: The polynomial hierarchy and a simple model for competitive analysis
jeroslow1985polynomial.abstract_or_role: Complexity of multilevel (competitive) programming: existence does not imply tractability.

lee2001fuzzy.title: Fuzzy and Multi-Level Decision Making: An Interactive Computational Approach
lee2001fuzzy.authors: Lee, E. Stanley and Shih, Hsu-Shih
lee2001fuzzy.abstract_or_role: Interactive fuzzy approaches to multi-level decision making.

cheng2019fuzzy.title: Fuzzy and Multi-Level Decision Making: Soft Computing Approaches
cheng2019fuzzy.authors: Cheng, Chi-Bin and Shih, Hsu-Shih and Lee, E. Stanley
cheng2019fuzzy.abstract_or_role: Updated soft-computing methods for fuzzy and multi-level decision making.

nash1951noncooperative.title: Non-Cooperative Games
nash1951noncooperative.abstract_or_role: Existence of mixed-strategy equilibrium in finite non-cooperative games; a boundary reference only, not a coupled generalised equilibrium.

jaffe1993geographic.title: Geographic Localization of Knowledge Spillovers as Evidenced by Patent Citations
jaffe1993geographic.authors: Jaffe, Adam B. and Trajtenberg, Manuel and Henderson, Rebecca
jaffe1993geographic.abstract_or_role: Patent citations as evidence of knowledge spillovers (flows), with a matched-control design.

alcacer2006patent.title: Patent Citations as a Measure of Knowledge Flows: The Influence of Examiner Citations
alcacer2006patent.abstract_or_role: Examiner-added citations make up a large share of patent citations and affect their use as measures of knowledge flow; inventor or applicant citations should be distinguished.

benjamini1995controlling.title: Controlling the False Discovery Rate: A Practical and Powerful Approach to Multiple Testing
benjamini1995controlling.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B (Methodological)
benjamini1995controlling.abstract_or_role: False discovery rate control (BH procedure) for multiple testing.

cohen1960coefficient.title: A Coefficient of Agreement for Nominal Scales
cohen1960coefficient.abstract_or_role: Cohen's kappa: chance-corrected agreement for nominal scales.

nosek2018preregistration.title: The preregistration revolution
nosek2018preregistration.authors: Nosek, Brian A. and Ebersole, Charles R. and DeHaven, Alexander C. and Mellor, David T.
nosek2018preregistration.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
nosek2018preregistration.abstract_or_role: Preregistration separates confirmatory from exploratory research by fixing the analysis plan before observing outcomes.

granovetter1985economic.title: Economic Action and Social Structure: The Problem of Embeddedness
granovetter1985economic.abstract_or_role: Economic action is embedded in concrete ongoing social relations. Background for locating integration problems inside organisations.

uspto2026patentsview.title: {PatentsView} granted patent disambiguated tables (dataset pvgpatdis), {USPTO} Open Data Portal
uspto2026patentsview.abstract_or_role: USPTO PatentsView granted-patent tables (pvgpatdis): patents, current CPC classifications, US patent citations and disambiguated assignees.

shrestha2019organizational.title: Organizational Decision-Making Structures in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
shrestha2019organizational.authors: Shrestha, Yash Raj and Ben-Menahem, Shiko M. and von Krogh, Georg
shrestha2019organizational.abstract_or_role: Organisational decision-making structures that combine humans and AI (full delegation to AI, sequential human-AI or AI-human decision-making, aggregated decision-making), and the decision-task conditions under which each fits.

raisch2021artificial.title: Artificial Intelligence and Management: The Automation--Augmentation Paradox
raisch2021artificial.abstract_or_role: Automation versus augmentation of managerial tasks with AI as a paradox; argues the two are interdependent across time and space and should be managed together.

jarrahi2018artificial.title: Artificial intelligence and the future of work: Human-{AI} symbiosis in organizational decision making
jarrahi2018artificial.abstract_or_role: Human-AI symbiosis in organisational decision making: AI is suited to complexity, while humans contribute where decisions involve uncertainty and equivocality.

berente2021managing.title: Managing Artificial Intelligence
berente2021managing.authors: Berente, Nicholas and Gu, Bin and Recker, Jan and Santhanam, Radhika
berente2021managing.abstract_or_role: Managing AI as the frontier of computing; the facets of autonomy, learning and inscrutability raise distinctive management challenges for information-systems research.

swanson1986fish.title: Fish Oil, {Raynaud's} Syndrome, and Undiscovered Public Knowledge
swanson1986fish.abstract_or_role: Literature-based discovery: links between literatures that are never co-cited or co-mentioned can point to undiscovered public knowledge; the absence of co-occurrence is used to generate hypotheses about connections.

callon1983translations.title: From translations to problematic networks: An introduction to co-word analysis
callon1983translations.authors: Callon, Michel and Courtial, Jean-Pierre and Turner, William A. and Bauin, Serge
callon1983translations.abstract_or_role: Co-word analysis: co-occurrence of keywords is used to map the structure of research fields and the relations, or lack of relations, between research themes.
